content:
Rachel Apa, 24, died after collapsing during her first marathon, the New York City Marathon, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, according to reports from the New York Times, the New York Post, and USA Today.

Apa collapsed at about 1:30 p.m. near the 24-mile mark in Central Park, about two miles from the finish line. A spectator, hospital social worker Michaela Nicholas, ran to help and gave CPR, and marathon medical staff used a defibrillator before paramedics took Apa by ambulance to Mount Sinai Medical Center.

Doctors worked for more than six hours to save her, her family said, and she was pronounced dead at about 9:40 p.m.

Her father, Steve Apa, told the New York Times that her cause of death was rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition in which muscles break down and their contents enter the bloodstream, which can be caused by exertion. He described his daughter as being in perfect health and perfect shape before the race.

Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University and was pursuing an MBA at Charleston Southern University. She was running her first marathon to raise money for the Parkinson's Foundation, in honor of her grandfather, who battled Parkinson's disease before his death in 2022.

New York Road Runners, which organizes the race, said in a statement that it was deeply saddened by Rachel's passing following running in Sunday's race. Organizers said the last time a runner died following a medical incident at the race was in 2024.

Sources: New York Times, as reported by the New York Post and USA Today; New York Road Runners statement; New York Daily News.

title: Rachel Apa, 24, dies after collapsing near mile 24 of her first New York City Marathon
